about_subtitle: An ongoing practice in music, sound and creation
about_note: Different sounds, different spaces, different ways of creating around music. Always driven by the same curiosity
about_paragraph_1:
Music has always been an open territory. A space for exploration, experimentation and discovery, without the need to belong to a particular genre, format or discipline.

Over more than two decades, this curiosity has taken many forms: from techno and ambient to classical music, from compositions for video games, theatre and sports to producing and mixing music for other artists. Different languages, different contexts, but always the same desire to explore what sound can become.

Composition, production, mixing, performing and DJing are not separate practices, but different ways of approaching the same creative process. Sometimes through the detail and intimacy of the studio, sometimes through the energy and unpredictability of a dancefloor. Each offers a different perspective, and each feeds the others.

Music also exists beyond the act of making it. Creating spaces, bringing people together and imagining environments where unexpected things can happen have become an essential part of this journey. A club, a festival or an intimate listening session can be as meaningful a creative expression as a composition or a record.

There is no single sound to pursue, no fixed direction to follow. Just an ongoing curiosity, an instinct to keep experimenting and a belief that music can take many forms.

One continuous practice.

spaces_subtitle: Sometimes making music means making room for it
spaces_description:
Creating spaces has become another way of expressing a musical vision. Places where sound, architecture, nature and people come together, and where the experience itself becomes part of the creative process.

Les Arcs is perhaps the most personal expression of this idea. More than a club, it is a living project, constantly evolving through music, shared experiences and the people who bring it to life.

Other projects, such as L’Estrany and COREA, have explored this same curiosity in different ways, each leaving its own stories, connections and memories
spaces_note: Different spaces. Different stories. The same curiosity
spaces_les_arcs_description:
Les Arcs Club

A truly one-of-a-kind space, Les Arcs is set within an 800-year-old Catalan farmhouse, surrounded by nature. A club with impeccable sound, where the intensity of electronic music meets the beauty and tranquility of the natural world.

More than a club, Les Arcs was conceived as a place for connection, experimentation and shared experiences. A meeting point for music, people and ideas, built around the belief that creating the right environment can be just as meaningful as creating the music itself.
spaces_lestrany_description:
L’ESTRANY - FESTIVAL DE MÚSICA INSÒLITA

For nine editions, this tiny festival transformed Pla de l’Estrany (Girona, Spain) into a place where music, people and imagination came together.

What made it truly special was the collective spirit of the people behind it, its extraordinary locations and the almost magical atmosphere that emerged in each space.

Driven by curiosity and an instinct for discovering new talent, the festival welcomed artists such as Rosalía, Orbe, Alizzz and Carles Viarnés long before they gained the recognition they enjoy today.

More than a festival, L’Estrany was a shared vision — a celebration of creativity, intuition and the belief that something extraordinary can happen when the right people come together in the right place.
spaces_corea_description:
COREA — ROBADORS 23

A serie of intimate DJ sessions held at the legendary Robadors 23, a small and welcoming venue in Barcelona’s Raval neighbourhood, deeply rooted in the city’s jazz and flamenco culture.

Bringing together some of the finest selectors from Barcelona and Catalonia, COREA offered each artist five hours to explore unexpected musical directions, take risks and build a journey beyond the conventions of a typical club set.

Artists such as Alicia Carrera, DJ Gus and Abu Sou were part of a project where musical curiosity, careful selection and the closeness between DJ and audience created something genuinely special.

More than a series of parties, COREA was a celebration of the art of listening, sharing music and letting it unfold naturally.
